model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, CET1 retention on risk-weighted-asset growth, AT1 and preference distributions charged in the flow

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E operating income, RMB m: H1 2026 actual 411,122 (interim, +11.2% YoY, helped by trading/investment gains) + H2 2026E ~368,900 (H2 2025 actual 355,338 x ~1.04). FY2025 actual 725,131. Revenue = net interest income + net fee and commission income + other non-interest income, the Bank's 'operating income' line. Operating income was flat FY2021-FY2025 (721,746 -> 725,131, 0.1% CAGR) while RWA grew ~8%/yr.
inputs.share_count_basis: 349,983,033,873 A + H ordinary shares on the register at 30 June 2026 (interim, dividend paragraph and EPS note; basic = diluted, SBC-zero) PLUS ~21,918m new A shares ASSUMED for the RMB160bn core-tier-1 private placement announced Sep-2026 (MOF RMB130bn; Analysis JSON recent_developments; the interim already refers to 'completion of the private placement of ordinary shares' and the preference-share conversion price adjusting 2.43 -> 2.46). Issue price is NOT disclosed in the filings held here: ASSUMED CNY 7.30/share, near the 601288.SS close of CNY 7.24 and ~11% below H1 2026 BVPS 8.17 (the 2025 round priced BOC/CCB/BOCOM/PSBC at ~10% premiums to market). Proceeds are credited in equity_bridge. Sensitivity is small: at CNY 7.00 the count is 372,840m, at 7.60 it is 371,036m (+/-0.25%). Replace with the placement circular's price and share number when published. Held FLAT thereafter: preference shares (RMB79.9bn) convert only on a CET1 trigger (5.125%), not modelled.
inputs.debt_cash_note: Bank: customer deposits (RMB32.6tn FY2025), interbank funding, central-bank borrowings (RMB1.13tn) and debt securities issued (RMB3.53tn at 30 Jun 2026) are operating funding; cash and central-bank balances are liquidity, not surplus. Net debt is zero by construction on the FCFE route; nothing is bridged after the flows except the placement proceeds.
inputs.fcf_note: last_fcf is FY2026E FCFE = net profit attributable to ORDINARY shareholders ~271bn (PBT ~343bn at 44.0% margin, less income tax, NCI and other-equity-instrument distributions at ~21%) LESS capital retained to hold CET1 at 10.8% on FY2026E RWA growth of ~8.8% (0.088 x 0.108 x 24,812,801 = ~236bn) = ~35-50bn; recorded at the midpoint 47bn. It is FAR BELOW the ~RMB91bn of ordinary dividends (FY2025 DPS RMB0.2495 x 349,983m) plus ~RMB17bn of AT1/preference coupons the Bank pays: CET1 fell 11.42% (FY2024) -> 11.08% (FY2025) -> 10.80% (H1 2026) and the RMB160bn MOF-led placement is what closes the gap. Reported OCF - capex (FY2025: 2,112,907 - 27,348) is deposit and interbank flow noise and is not used.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero: no share-based payment scheme disclosed in the FY2018-FY2025 annual reports (ShareRepurchases 0 and StockBasedComp 0 in every period of the CSV); basic = diluted EPS (RMB0.78 FY2025, RMB0.40 H1 2026). House and street bases coincide; band_position is degenerate.
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate converts CNY (model; the Bank reports in RMB) to HKD (H-share quote): CNYHKD=X 1.1732 at 2026-10-16T07:54Z, Yahoo Finance. Triangulated against USDCNY=X 6.6859 / USDHKD=X 7.8475 = 1.1738 (same source, same day). The Shanghai A share (601288.SS) closed at CNY 7.24 = HKD 8.49, a ~26% A/H premium that is normal for Chinese state banks, so the dual listing is not a parity check. Per-share values are per ordinary share and apply equally to A and H shares.
inputs.fy0: FY2026E (year ending 2026-12-31, unreported: H1 2026 actual + H2 estimate)
inputs.cet1_anchor: CET1 ratio 10.80% on RWA RMB26,281,608m at 30 Jun 2026 (interim p.7, lines 411-471); 11.08% on 24,812,801m at FY2025; 11.42% on 22,603,866m at FY2024. Net CET1 capital 2,838,783m; AT1 470,000m; total CAR 17.50%. RWA grew 11.3% FY2022, 12.5% FY2023, 1.2% FY2024 (new capital rules), 9.8% FY2025, 5.9% in H1 2026 alone. G-SIB bucket 1: minimum CET1 ~8.5% (5% + 2.5% conservation + 1% G-SIB), so the buffer is ~2.3pt.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single CNY cost of equity 9.5% in every scenario (risk is charged once, through the scenario weights, not by moving the discount rate). Built in the flows' own currency: 10-year China Government Bond ~1.8% (ASSUMPTION: not fetched; the PBOC easing cycle has had the 10Y CGB in the 1.6-2.0% range since 2025) + beta ~1.0 x China ERP ~6.5% = ~8.3%, plus ~1.2pt for risks a CSI-300 ERP does not price for an H-share holder: state-directed lending under rural revitalisation and the 'Five Priorities', the thinnest NIM of the Big Four (1.28% H1 2026), the highest property-sector NPL ratio of the Big Four, majority MOF/Huijin control with recurring below-book recapitalisations and no buyback lever, and capital-account/RMB convertibility risk. Same 9.5% as the sibling Big Four name 0939.HK (CCB); one point BELOW the 10.5% used for the joint-stock bank 0998.HK (CITIC), the differential being the state-bank/G-SIB funding and support premium. Hurdle for entry price is the house 15%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Bank: IFRS 16 right-of-use depreciation and lease-liability interest (RMB10,495m lease liabilities at FY2025, AR line 14792) sit inside operating expenses, i.e. inside the pre-tax margin. lease_cost_pct_path is zero so the charge is not taken twice; nothing is deducted as debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, inside the 'cash_tax_rate' deduction: the margin is calibrated to PROFIT BEFORE TAX (323,689 FY2025, after credit impairment 127,189) and the deduction rate covers income tax, profit attributable to non-controlling interests and distributions on other equity instruments (AT1 perpetual bonds + preference shares). FY2025: tax 31,686 (9.8% effective, tax-exempt CGB/local-government-bond interest) + NCI 962 (0.3%) + other-equity distributions 17,085 (5.3%) = 15.4% of PBT, leaving 273,956 to ordinary shareholders (EPS 0.78 x 349,983m = 272,987 cross-check). H1 2026: tax 33,707 (18.5% effective, unexplained in the MD&A beyond the usual bond-exemption boilerplate) + NCI 1,681 (0.9%) + other-equity 6,821 (3.8%) = 23.2%. The paths sit between the two vintages at 21% (base). Other equity instruments (RMB470,000m) and NCI (RMB6,189m) are therefore NOT deducted again in a bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> dcf-methods routing row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker, thrift'. Run as FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, the house precedent for banks (HSBC, LYG, WF, MFG, HDB, IBN, BMO, USB, WFC, NAB.AX, 0939.HK, 0998.HK). First valuation of this ticker, no MEMORY.md entry. Not an owner-FCF DCF: deposits are operating funding, OCF is meaningless (swings from -61bn to +2,113bn), net debt is zero by construction and no debt or cash is bridged. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = operating income; ebitda_margin = pre-tax profit margin (after credit impairment, which is the real cost of a bank); sbc, D&A, leases and working capital all zero; cash_tax_rate = income tax + NCI + AT1/preference distributions, so EBIT x (1 - rate) = net profit to ORDINARY shareholders; capex = equity retained to hold CET1 at 10.8% on RWA growth (g_RWA x 10.8% x prior-year RWA, as % of revenue), so FCF = FCFE = distributable earnings. Terminal growth applies to FCFE at the cost of equity; terminal_cap_multiple 18x FCFE is above the Gordon multiple in every scenario (15.8x base, 17.3x bull, 14.6x bear) and does not bind. KEY FINDING: FY2026E FCFE ~RMB47bn is roughly HALF the ~RMB91bn ordinary dividend; the 31% payout is being funded by CET1 drift (11.42% -> 10.80% in 18 months) and by the state (RMB160bn placement). The valuation credits only the FCFE plus the placement cash, and lets FCFE rise as RWA growth decelerates from ~9% toward 3%. The bear case is close to the FY2022-2025 status quo (flat revenue, RWA +9-12%/yr) and in it FCFE is negative for FY2027-28, i.e. a further dilutive recapitalisation. QUALITATIVE CONTEXT (1288.HK_Analysis.json, 2026-10-16): NIM 1.28% H1 2026 (-4bp YoY, +2bp QoQ, first sign of stabilisation after 2.12% FY2021 -> 1.60% FY2023); NPL 1.25% (improving 5 years), coverage ~290%; cost-to-income 35.2% FY2025; County Area loans +9.0% H1 to RMB11.9tn (41.9% of domestic loans); net profit +5.8% H1 2026; interim DPS RMB0.1297 (31.0% payout); DBS target HKD 7.10 (Sep-2026). Valuation date is 9.5 months into FY2026, so FY2026E is fy0 (not discounted) and the first discounted flow is FY2027; the FY2025 final dividend (45.5bn, May 2026) and FY2026 interim (45.4bn, H2 2026) are paid out of fy0 and are not double-counted. The H share trades at 0.70x H1 2026 BVPS (RMB8.17 = HKD 9.58) and a 4.3% FY2025 dividend yield.

equity_bridge.item: RMB160bn core-tier-1 private placement proceeds (MOF RMB130bn), announced Sep-2026, not on the 30 Jun 2026 balance sheet
equity_bridge.note: Matches the ~21,918m new shares in shares_outstanding at an ASSUMED CNY 7.30 issue price. Cash raised offsets the CET1 retention the flows charge; without it the model would deduct the same capital twice (once as retention, once as dilution with no proceeds). Remove both the bridge and the extra shares if the placement lapses.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: operating-income growth with NIM stabilising at ~1.3% and balance-sheet growth of 5-7% slowing; above the 1.4-1.9% revenue CAGRs (NIM compression years) and below the 7.5-8.0% ordinary-equity CAGR, which is retained capital, not earnings power
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Ordinary-equity CAGR (8.0% 5yr) exceeds revenue CAGR (1.9%) by >30%: book value compounds from retained profit and the FY2018 placement while operating income was flat FY2021-25, so ROE has fallen from 14.6% (FY2017) to ~10% (FY2025). Book-value growth must NOT be used as the growth rate for a bank whose NI/RWA is falling.
historical_growth.notes: 'fcf' CAGRs are net profit attributable to ORDINARY shareholders (FY2020 206,395 -> FY2025 273,956; FY2022 241,993), the FCFE numerator; reported FCF is deposit-flow noise for a bank. Revenue = operating income FY2020 659,332 / FY2022 695,283 / FY2025 725,131. EPS RMB0.59 (FY2020), 0.69 (FY2022), 0.78 (FY2025). Ordinary shareholders' equity (excl. other equity instruments) FY2020 1,884,910 / FY2022 2,228,060 / FY2025 2,767,180; BVPS 5.39 / 6.37 / 7.91.

base.growth_rationale: Operating income +3.5% for four years then 3.0%: NIM stabilising at ~1.25-1.30% (deposit repricing of the maturing high-cost time-deposit stock offsets asset-yield declines; H1 2026 +2bp QoQ), loans growing 7-9% slowing to 3-4%, fee income flat-to-up after the H1 2026 one-off base effect. Below RWA growth in the early years, so NI/RWA keeps drifting down (1.10% FY2025 -> ~0.85% terminal).
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax margin after credit impairment. FY2023 44.2%, FY2024 44.9%, FY2025 44.6%, H1 2026 44.2%, FY2026E 44.0%. Base holds 43.5%: credit cost ~0.5% of loans (FY2025 127bn on 26.2tn), cost-to-income ~35%, no NIM recovery, property/LGFV provisioning absorbed within the ~290% coverage buffer.
base.capex_rationale: Equity retained to hold CET1 at 10.8% on RWA growth of 7.5%, 7.0, 6.5, 6.0, 5.5, 5.0, 4.5, 4.0, 3.5, 3.0 from FY2026E RWA RMB27,000bn (FY2025 24,813bn, H1 2026 26,282bn; H2 assumed +2.7%). The interim says the Bank 'strengthened total capital constraint ... controlled the growth of risk-weighted assets', and County Area / Five Priorities lending keeps loan growth above system. Retention / revenue: 0.075 x 0.108 x 27,000,000 / 807,300 = 27.1% in FY2027, falling to 13.2% as RWA growth converges on terminal growth. Terminal-year RWA ~RMB45.0tn, CET1 ~RMB4,860bn; terminal ROE ~7.5%, implied terminal P/B ~0.7x = (ROE - g)/(CoE - g).
base.tax_rationale: Income tax ~16% (between FY2025's 9.8% and H1 2026's 18.5%; the H1 jump is not explained in the MD&A and may be one-off, so neither vintage is taken at face value) + NCI ~0.5% + other-equity-instrument distributions ~4.5% (RMB17,085m FY2025 on a larger PBT) = 21% of PBT, held flat. Coupons on the RMB470bn of AT1/preference instruments are fixed in RMB, so the percentage falls slightly as PBT grows; ignored (conservative).
base.terminal_note: Gordon on FY2036 FCFE at 9.5% - 3.0% = 15.8x; the 18x cap does not bind. It binds only in the sensitivity grid's low cost-of-equity rows, which is the cap doing its job: a bank earning ~7.5% on equity is not worth 20x+ its distributable earnings.

bull.growth_rationale: NIM recovers modestly to ~1.4% as deposit repricing runs ahead of asset-yield declines (S&P: sector margins bottom by 2027), County Area and private-enterprise lending keep volume growth at 8-9%, wealth-management fees recover with capital markets.
bull.margin_rationale: Credit cost falls to ~0.4% as the property book stabilises (NPL already down five years running, coverage ~290% allows provision release), cost-to-income back to ~33% on AI/digital efficiency; 46.5% is ~2pt above the FY2024 peak of 44.9%.
bull.capex_rationale: CET1 held at 10.8% on RWA growth of 6.5, 6.0, 5.5, 5.0, 4.5, 4.0, 3.5, 3.5, 3.0, 3.0% (advanced-approach RWA savings and asset-structure optimisation let revenue grow faster than RWA). Terminal RWA ~RMB41.7tn; terminal ROE ~9.5%.
bull.tax_rationale: Fixed AT1/preference coupons fall to ~3.5% of a larger PBT; effective tax ~16%.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon 1.035/0.06 = 17.3x FCFE; cap 18x does not bind.

bear.growth_rationale: The FY2021-FY2025 pattern repeats: NIM falls another 15-20bp (further LPR cuts in a deflationary macro, CPI +1.0%), fee income does not recover, and operating income is flat for two more years before growing ~2%. Policy-directed volume growth continues but earns nothing at the margin.
bear.margin_rationale: Credit cost rises to ~0.9-1.0% of loans in FY2027-28 (property developers where ABC carries the highest Big Four NPL ratio, LGFV restructuring, inclusive/retail finance) - the FY2020 COVID margin was 40.2% at a lower loan book - then partly recovers to 38%.
bear.capex_rationale: Policy-directed lending keeps RWA growing 8.0, 7.0, 6.0, 5.5, 5.0, 4.5, 4.0, 3.5, 3.0, 3.0% while earnings fall; CET1 held at 10.8% consumes MORE than ordinary profit in FY2027-28 (FCFE negative, ~RMB -30bn, against a ~RMB90bn dividend). In practice this is the scenario where a second below-book state recapitalisation dilutes the H share or the payout is cut; the flat share count understates the damage. Terminal RWA ~RMB43.7tn; terminal ROE ~5.6%.
bear.tax_rationale: Fixed AT1/preference coupons against a smaller PBT; H1 2026's 18.5% effective tax rate proves structural.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon 1.025/0.07 = 14.6x FCFE; cap does not bind. FY2027-28 FCFE are negative: the engine's zero floor applies to the terminal value only, and the terminal year is positive.

scenario_narratives.base: ABC remains what it is: a state-directed, deposit-rich Big Four bank whose NIM has stopped falling at ~1.3% and whose loan book grows 7-9% a year on County Area, inclusive and 'Five Priorities' lending. Operating income grows 3-3.5%, the pre-tax margin holds ~43.5% with credit cost ~0.5%, and CET1 is held at 10.8% on RWA decelerating from 7.5% to 3%. Because RWA grows faster than earnings for the first half of the horizon, FCFE starts at roughly half the dividend and only overtakes it around FY2030; the RMB160bn MOF placement bridges the gap. Terminal ROE ~7.5% against a 9.5% cost of equity implies a terminal P/B of ~0.7x, i.e. the H share is roughly fairly priced today at 0.70x book.
scenario_narratives.bull: Deposit repricing drives a real NIM recovery to ~1.4% by FY2028 while property-sector provisioning normalises down, so the pre-tax margin reaches 46.5% and operating income grows 4-5%. Advanced-approach RWA savings let CET1 hold at 10.8% with less retention, FCFE exceeds the dividend from FY2027, and terminal ROE of ~9.5% supports a terminal P/B near 1.0x. This is the sell-side 'margin trough is in' case plus a multi-year credit-cost tailwind.
scenario_narratives.bear: Deflation keeps the LPR falling, NIM slips below 1.1%, operating income is flat for two more years and the property/LGFV cycle lifts credit cost toward 1% of loans, compressing the pre-tax margin to 36%. Meanwhile the policy mandate keeps RWA growing 7-8%, so holding CET1 at 10.8% consumes more than ordinary profit in FY2027-28: FCFE is negative, the dividend is paid out of capital, and a second discounted state recapitalisation dilutes H-share holders. Terminal ROE ~5.6% implies a terminal P/B of ~0.45x. This is the FY2022-2025 status quo extended, not a tail event.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 30% (above the house default 15%, equal to the 30% used for sibling Big Four name 0939.HK/CCB, below the 35% for joint-stock 0998.HK): the bear case is close to ABC's own FY2022-2025 trajectory (flat operating income, RWA +9-12%/yr, CET1 drifting, dividend above FCFE, state recapitalisations), NIM is the thinnest of the Big Four at 1.28%, property NPLs are the highest of the Big Four, and H1 2026's effective tax rate doubled without explanation; the state backstop caps solvency risk but not dilution risk, which is why bear is not higher. Bull 20%: NIM has only just stopped falling, fee income fell 8.7% in H1 2026, and the policy-lending mandate caps the margin upside. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is worth the equity cash flow it can distribute after funding its own capital requirement, discounted at the cost of equity. For Agricultural Bank of China that flow is net profit to ordinary shareholders (after tax, NCI, preference dividends and perpetual-bond coupons) less the equity retained to hold CET1 at 10.8% on growing risk-weighted assets. Today that FCFE (~RMB47bn) is roughly half the ~RMB91bn ordinary dividend, so the headline 4.3% yield is financed by capital-ratio drift and by the Ministry of Finance's RMB160bn placement; the model credits only the FCFE plus the placement cash and lets FCFE rise as RWA growth decelerates. Net debt is zero by construction; deposits are operating funding. The H share trades at 0.70x H1 2026 book; the base terminal P/B is ~0.7x, consistent with a ~7.5% ROE at a 9.5% cost of equity.
key_risks_to_valuation: CET1 target: holding 10.8% is the single largest driver. Allowing a drift to 10.0% (still ~1.5pt above the G-SIB minimum) would release ~RMB216bn once and add ~CNY 0.5/share; a regulator-driven rise to 11.5% would subtract the same.

RWA growth path: every 1pt of extra annual RWA growth costs ~RMB29bn of FCFE per year (0.01 x 0.108 x 27tn). ABC's policy mandate (County Area loans growing faster than the book) makes the deceleration assumption the main judgment.
Deduction rate: the FY2025 (15.4%) vs H1 2026 (23.2%) spread on tax + NCI + AT1 coupons is worth ~CNY 0.7/share in the base case; the paths use 21%.

Placement terms: issue price and share count are assumed (CNY 7.30, ~21.9bn shares); the per-share effect of a different price is small (+/-0.25% on the count) but a larger or repeated below-book raise would dilute further.
Credit cost: ABC's property NPL ratio is the highest of the Big Four; a 0.5pt rise in credit cost on a RMB27tn loan book is ~RMB135bn of pre-tax profit, roughly the base-to-bear margin gap.
NIM: at a 1.28% margin on RMB48tn of interest-earning assets, every 5bp is ~RMB24bn of operating income (~3%).
Currency: the H share is quoted in HKD against RMB flows; a 5% RMB depreciation against the HKD-pegged USD moves every HKD value 5% with no change to the business.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (1288.HK) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range HKD 5.08-6.815. CNY/HKD from CNYHKD=X, triangulated via USDCNY=X and USDHKD=X; 601288.SS A-share close for the A/H premium.
data_sources.financials: 1288.HK_Metrics.csv and kpis (core_metrics) from the FY2018-FY2025 annual reports and the H1 2024-H1 2026 interim reports; H1 2026 interim (research/1288.HK/Extracted/1288.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt) for CET1/RWA (lines 405-475), dividends (4972-4995), EPS note (6372-6390), tax (1037-1042), preference-share conversion-price adjustment on the placement (8652-8665); FY2025 annual for the other-equity distributions (line 9590), lease liabilities (14792), effective tax rate (1707-1710).
